case_name: Abdul Rashid Abdul Rahiman Patel and Others v State Of Maharashtra
petitioner: Abdul Rashid Abdul Rahiman Patel and Others
respondent:
State Of Maharashtra
Supreme Court of India

10 July 2007
Appeal (crl.) 9 of 2001 WITH CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 504 OF 2000 AND CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 60 OF 2001
The Judgment was delivered by : B. N. Agrawal, J.
1.  Seventeen accused persons were charged and tried for offences under Sections 147, 148, 302/149, 302 read with Section 34, 307/149, 326/149 and 324/149 of the Indian Penal Code ['IPC' for short] and by judgment rendered by the Trial Court they were acquitted of all the charges. Against the order of acquittal an appeal was preferred by the State of Maharashtra before the High Court during the pendency of which Abbas Yunus Sonde [A-8] and Ibrahim alias Abdul Rahman Mohammad Kasim Patel [A-9] died, as such, appeal against them abated. facts: The Seventeen accused persons were charged and tried for offences under Sections 147, 148, 302/149, 302 read with Section 34, 307/149, 326/149 and 324/149 of the Indian Penal Code ['IPC' for short] and by judgment rendered by the Trial Court they were acquitted of all the charges.
One Mariam, daughter of Usman Hasanmiya [PW 19] had love affair with Qasim Hasanmiya Bedekar [A-7].
Prosecution case was that one Mariam disappeared from the village along with A-7. They proceeded to Bombay and got married on 15.08.1982.

There was tension between the two groups in the village, i.e., Bedekars (accused persons) and Jalgaonkars (the members of prosecution party) on account of their said love affair but the matter was settled.
Salma Usman Dhanse [PW-12] had spread rice on the road in front of her house for drying. She had asked her daughter Parvin to sit and watch the same.
Hajirabai [A-16], who was living in the vicinity, thought that Salma had made those remarks against her, as such she picked up a quarrel with Salma.
Usman Abdul Rahiman Dhanse [PW-3], husband of Salma, was coming to his house, A-16 accosted him and conveyed her grievance against Salma.
Nijam Malang Mukadam [PW-4], brother of PW-12, enquired as to why they were quarrelling, the four accused persons also abused and threatened him.
Prosecution witnesses were also sitting in the house of Ismail who advised PW-3 and PW-4 not to quarrel but to lodge a complaint with the police.
The Police obtained a written undertaking from the parties to the above effect.
All the accused persons armed with swords, iron bars and sticks were waiting near a well for the return of the Jalgaonkars, i.e., the members of prosecution party.
A-1 to A-5, A-8 and A-10 were armed with swords.
Israil was seen coming behind PW-4. Therefore, the accused persons turned towards Ismail.
Ismail came to be attacked near the tamarind tree. A-1, A-2, A-3, A-4 and A-10 dealt sword blows on the head of Ismail.
Suleman reached near him and tried to save him from the accused persons.
Yusuf also reached there who was also attacked by A-2, A-3, A-5 and A-10 as a result of which he fell down.
PW-12 also reached there and was also assaulted by some of the accused.

When this was going on, PW-2 thought of reporting the matter to the police and accordingly, he came to the Bombay-Pune road, boarded a taxi, reached Khalapur Police Station and informed the Station In-charge, Shivaji Dhondu Pawar [PW-37] at 2:45 in the night that A-1 was moving with a sword in the village and was indulging in massacre and there was great commotion in the village.

Police after registering the case took up investigation and on completion thereof submitted charge sheet, on receipt whereof the learned Magistrate took cognizance and committed the seventeen accused persons to the Court of Sessions to face trial.
issues: The legal questions or points of law being debated
petitioner_arguments: Shri Shekhar Naphade, the learned senior counsel appearing on behalf of the appellants in Criminal Appeal No. 504 of 2000, in support of the appeal, submitted that the prosecution failed to prove its case and participation of the appellants in the crime by credible evidence.

Shri S.K. Aggrawal, learned senior counsel appearing on behalf of the appellants in Criminal Appeal No. 9 of 2001, submitted that the High Court was not justified in convicting A-5, A-6 and A-11 under Sections 148 and 324/149 IPC.

Learned counsel then submitted that out of these appellants, A-5 and A-6 have already undergone the sentences imposed upon them and have been released from custody, but so far as A-11 is concerned, he has remained in custody for a period of 15 months, as such the sentences of imprisonment awarded against him should be reduced to the period already undergone.
court_reasoning: The learned Magistrate took cognizance and committed the seventeen accused persons to the Court of Sessions to face trial.
The High Court partly reversed the order of acquittal and convicted eight accused persons as stated above.
The Trial Court acquitted all the accused persons but on appeal being preferred High Court partly reversed the order of acquittal and convicted eight accused persons as stated above.
